questions.question: Why should functions usually return values instead of only printing?
options: Returned values are easier to test and reuse.
Printing is not allowed in Python.
Return statements make code run in parallel.
Printing changes the type of the value.
questions.explanation: A returned value can be asserted in tests and reused by other functions.

questions.question: What problem can `def add_item(item, items=[])` cause?
options: Python does not allow lists as defaults.
The default list is shared across calls and can retain old values.
The function will always return an empty list.
The function cannot accept more than one argument.
questions.explanation: Mutable defaults are evaluated once at definition time, not per call.

questions.question: What is the difference between a parameter and an argument?
options: Parameters are always strings.
They are the same thing.
A parameter is in the function definition; an argument is the value passed at call time.
Arguments are only keyword values.
questions.explanation: Parameters describe inputs, arguments provide concrete values.

questions.question: What does `*args` do in a function signature?
options: Prevents default arguments.
Collects keyword arguments into a dictionary.
Requires all arguments to be keyword-only.
Collects extra positional arguments into a tuple.

questions.question: What does a function return if there is no return statement?
options: None
An empty string
It raises NameError.
questions.explanation: Python returns `None` when no explicit return value is provided.

questions.question: Why can keyword arguments improve readability?
options: They force Python to infer types.
They make argument intent explicit at call sites.
They run faster than positional arguments.
They prevent defaults from being used.
questions.explanation: Named arguments document intent, especially with many optional parameters.

questions.question: When should you split a function into smaller functions?
options: When the function has exactly one parameter.
When the function uses return.
When one function handles multiple unrelated responsibilities.
Never; larger functions are always better.
questions.explanation: Single-responsibility functions are easier to test and maintain.

questions.question: What is the main value of a docstring?
options: It turns dynamic typing into static typing.
It makes code execute faster.
It replaces tests.
It explains behavior and usage for humans and tools.
questions.explanation: Docstrings improve readability and can be surfaced by help/tooling.
